title: Utilization Management Clinical Policy: Level of Care Adjudication for Acute Chest Pain / Rule-Out ACS
regulatory_framework: CMS Two-Midnight Rule (CMS-1599-F; 42 CFR § 412.3) / MCG Care Guidelines / InterQual
summary: Establishes clinical criteria determining whether acute chest pain qualifies for Part A Acute Inpatient Admission versus Part B Observation Stay. Inpatient admission requires acute high-risk features or unexpected clinical deterioration spanning 2 midnights.

criteria.name: Hemodynamic Instability or Cardiogenic Shock
criteria.description: Sustained SBP < 90 mmHg, requiring vasopressors, acute pulmonary edema, or life-threatening ventricular arrhythmia.
criteria.statutory_reference: AHA/ACC 2021 Chest Pain Guideline Section 4; CMS Two-Midnight Exception

criteria.name: Positive Serial Cardiac Biomarkers (Acute Myocardial Infarction)
criteria.description: Documented rising and/or falling cardiac troponin above the 99th percentile upper reference limit (URL) consistent with acute myocardial necrosis.
criteria.statutory_reference: Fourth Universal Definition of Myocardial Infarction; MCG Inpatient Indicators

criteria.name: New Ischemic ECG Changes (ST Elevation or Persistent ST Depression)
criteria.description: New ST-segment elevation >= 1mm in two contiguous leads, dynamic ST depressions >= 1mm, or new pathological Q waves.

criteria.name: Physician Expectation of Two or More Midnights of Hospital Care
criteria.description: Admitting physician must explicitly document medical necessity rationale why patient requires acute hospital-level interventions expected to span across at least two midnights.

groups.title: Acute High-Risk Objective Clinical Severity (Must satisfy at least 1 for Inpatient)
